metadata.rules_text:
- When sentiment is consistently negative (especially >15 days), model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction by 2–5% of forecasted value.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior period), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast by 3–8% in next 3–5 periods.
- If recent history shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive downward moves), model tends to ignore trend; adjust forecast to align with recent 5-day average.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to neutral/positive, model often underreacts; increase forecast by 1–3% to capture sentiment-driven rebound.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently underestimates volatility in high-sentiment periods; add 1–2% volatility buffer if sentiment >0.3.
- If true outcome deviates >10% from 14-day moving average, model is likely misaligned with underlying trend; re-calibrate using 14-day MA as anchor.
